anlamlar.en: to move away from someone, or to stop trying to force someone to do something
ornekler: Back off! Leave me alone.
The reporters backed off when the police arrived.

anlamlar.en: to become successful or healthy again after a difficult period
ornekler: The economy bounced back quickly.
She bounced back after losing the first set.

anlamlar.en: to cause something to happen
ornekler: The internet has brought about huge changes.
What brought about this decision?

anlamlar.en: to bring someone or something with you
ornekler: Bring along your friends!
Don't forget to bring along a pen.

anlamlar.en: to return with something, or to return something
ornekler: Can you bring back some bread?
Please bring my book back tomorrow.

anlamlar.en: to make you remember something
ornekler: This photo brings back happy memories.
The song brought back my school days.

anlamlar.en: to start doing or using something again
ornekler: The school brought back uniforms.
Some people want to bring back the old rules.

anlamlar.en: to reduce the level of something
ornekler: The government wants to bring down prices.
This medicine will bring down your temperature.

anlamlar.en: to make a government or leader lose power
ornekler: The scandal brought down the government.
Protests brought down the president.

anlamlar.en: to change the date or time of an event so that it happens earlier
ornekler: The meeting has been brought forward to Monday.
Can we bring the exam forward a week?

anlamlar.en: to introduce a new law or system
ornekler: The government brought in a new tax.
They're bringing in stricter rules.

anlamlar.en: to earn or make money
ornekler: The shop brings in about $2,000 a week.
Tourism brings in a lot of money.

anlamlar.en: to produce something and start to sell it
ornekler: The band is bringing out a new album.
They brought out a new model last year.

anlamlar.en: to make a quality or detail easier to notice
ornekler: The sun brings out the colors of the garden.
Difficult times bring out the best in people.

anlamlar.en: to look after a child until it becomes an adult
ornekler: She was brought up by her grandparents.
They brought up four children.

anlamlar.en: to start to talk about a particular subject
ornekler: She brought up the question of money.
Don't bring up politics at dinner.

anlamlar.en: to practice and improve your skills or knowledge of something you learned in the past
ornekler: I need to brush up on my French before the trip.
She's brushing up on her math.

anlamlar.en: to find out what someone is doing to make sure they are behaving correctly
ornekler: My parents are always checking up on me.
The boss checks up on us every hour.

anlamlar.en: to shout loudly to encourage someone in a competition
ornekler: The crowd cheered on the runners.
Come and cheer us on!

anlamlar.en: to give some money when several people are giving money to pay for something
ornekler: We all chipped in to buy her a present.
If everyone chips in $5, we'll have enough.

anlamlar.en: to interrupt a conversation to say something
ornekler: "That's not fair," she chipped in.
Feel free to chip in with ideas.

anlamlar.en: to eat, drink or use less of something
ornekler: I'm trying to cut down on coffee.
We need to cut down on plastic.

anlamlar.en: to slowly disappear or become weaker
ornekler: The sound of the music faded away.
Her smile faded away.

anlamlar.en: to defend yourself when someone attacks or criticizes you
ornekler: When he hit her, she fought back.
The team fought back to win 3–2.

anlamlar.en: to try hard not to show an emotion
ornekler: She fought back her tears.
He fought back his anger.

anlamlar.en: to delay doing something
ornekler: Let's hold off on buying a car until next year.
They held off making a decision.

anlamlar.en: to solve small problems or difficulties
ornekler: We need to iron out a few problems before we start.
The details still need to be ironed out.

anlamlar.en: to write something quickly
ornekler: Let me jot down your number.
She jotted down a few ideas.

anlamlar.en: to start to have an effect
ornekler: The painkillers are starting to kick in.
The new law kicks in next month.

anlamlar.en: to start to sleep, especially when sitting
ornekler: Grandpa nodded off in his chair.
I nodded off during the lecture.

anlamlar.en: to discover or describe exactly what something is
ornekler: It's hard to pin down the cause of the problem.
Scientists still can't pin down the date.

anlamlar.en: to make someone give clear details or make a decision
ornekler: I tried to pin him down to a date.
She's hard to pin down.

anlamlar.en: to keep money so that you can buy something in the future
ornekler: I'm saving up for a new bike.
She saved up for months to buy a laptop.

anlamlar.en: to start doing something
ornekler: She set about cleaning the house.
How do you set about finding a job?

anlamlar.en: to begin and seem likely to continue (something unpleasant)
ornekler: Winter seems to have set in early.
Panic set in when we realized we were lost.

anlamlar.en: to accept something that is not what you really want
ornekler: We wanted a house, but we settled for a small apartment.
Don't settle for second best.

anlamlar.tr: (en uygununu bulmak için) farklı yerlere bakmak
anlamlar.en: to compare prices in different shops before you buy something
ornekler: It's worth shopping around for a good price.
Shop around before you choose a bank.

anlamlar.en: to be completely understood after some time
ornekler: It took a while for the news to sink in.
It still hasn't sunk in that I won.

anlamlar.en: to make a mistake
ornekler: Someone slipped up and sent the wrong letter.
If you slip up, you'll lose points.

anlamlar.en: to move or happen faster, or to make something do this
ornekler: The car sped up as it went down the hill.
We need to speed up the process.

anlamlar.en: to explain something in a very clear way with details
ornekler: Do I have to spell it out for you?
The contract spells out the conditions.

anlamlar.en: to increase the size, amount or speed of something
ornekler: The police have stepped up security.
We need to step up our efforts.

anlamlar.en: to buy a lot of something to use later
ornekler: We stocked up on food before the storm.
Stock up on water for the trip.

anlamlar.en: to make someone feel very worried or nervous
ornekler: Exams really stress me out.
Don't stress out about it.

anlamlar.en: to add more of something to make it full again
ornekler: I need to top up my phone.
Can I top up your glass?

anlamlar.en: to find someone or something after looking for them in a lot of places
ornekler: The police tracked down the killer.
I finally tracked down the book I wanted.

anlamlar.en: to think carefully about the good and bad parts of a situation before deciding
ornekler: You need to weigh up the pros and cons.
She weighed up her options.

anlamlar.en: to accept that an amount of money has been lost or will not be paid back
ornekler: The bank wrote off the debt.
They had to write off the loss.

anlamlar.en: to decide that someone or something is not useful or will not succeed
ornekler: Don't write him off yet.
Everyone had written the team off.

anlamlar.en: to write something in a complete form, usually using notes you made earlier
ornekler: I need to write up my notes from the lecture.
She wrote up the results of the experiment.

anlamlar.en: to make the image of something appear smaller, to see more of it, with a camera or on a screen
ornekler: Zoom out to see the whole map.
The camera zoomed out slowly.
